criteria.commensurate: Yes, overall. Summed over 16 runs the end is faster (bookend 112.0 -> 107.8 s; homesteads, notice and the main leg all down), and the entrance boards are back on 16 of 16. One seed crosses: 20 hh seed 25 at +11.1%, serial 6.39 -> 6.8-7.0 s.
criteria.necessary: Yes. The GM ordered the pre-seating ways removed (amendment 2), so the field way has to be searched after the houses (settle_field). Disabled at 356ccaf8c, 20/25 refuses with the field unreached. The rest of 20/25's web growth (+0.6 s) is the skeleton and tree routing round this seed's new house layout. Summed over 16 runs it nets about +0.7 s (web minus settle_field 13.4 -> 14.1 s), so it swings with the layout and is not new work.
criteria.no_way_around: No. A cheap, output-identical fix exists for the larger part of settle_field. checks.ford_crossing is called 2,408 times from corridors.field_runs on 20/25. Each call tests the straight run against every brook leg (484k segments_cross), and the brook does not change during the scan. Filtering the legs by bounding box first is exact, because segments_cross needs overlapping boxes; cache the legs and boxes on the hashable brook tuple. Prototyped as a monkeypatch: 16 of 16 maps hash-identical, 20/25 settle_field 0.33 -> 0.13 s, web 1.28 -> 1.08 s, total about 6.77 -> 6.57 s against the start's 6.39 s. The last audit recommended this without blocking on it; on the seed that crossed it is 60% of settle_field. Apply it and re-bookend.
